urgency.h: While You're Grieving, Their Insurer Is Working
urgency.sub: You should be able to focus on your family. Unfortunately, the people responsible are already focused on limiting what they owe.

cards.t: The early call from the insurer
cards.p: It sounds like sympathy. It's a settlement attempt — made while you're least able to think about numbers. Anything you sign in those weeks closes the claim forever.
Vehicles get scrapped. Footage gets overwritten. Witnesses scatter. A lawyer can preserve all of it now, so you don't have to think about it.
California gives families a window to file — and if a government agency was involved, it can be as short as six months. We'll handle the timeline so you don't have to carry it.

result_highlight: California's wrongful death law lets a surviving spouse, children, and other dependents recover for lost financial support, funeral and medical costs, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance — and, through the estate, the pain your loved one suffered. We build these cases with the resources of one of the state's largest injury firms.

value.h: The Law Cannot Undo It. It Can Make Sure Your Family Is Provided For.
value.sub: These are the damages California law makes available to the family of someone killed by negligence.

items.p: The income, benefits, and household contributions your loved one would have provided over a lifetime — calculated by economic experts, not by an adjuster.
Burial costs and any medical bills from the final injury or illness.
California allows families to recover for the relationship itself — the care, comfort, protection, and guidance that was taken from a spouse, a child, a parent.
Through the estate, the pain and suffering your loved one endured before passing, and — where the conduct was reckless — punitive damages to punish it.

A trucking company that pushed a driver past his limits. A property owner who ignored a hazard for months. A verdict says out loud what happened — and makes it less likely to happen to the next family.

faq.q: Who can file a wrongful death claim in California?
faq.a: Generally the surviving spouse or domestic partner, children, and — if there are none — other heirs such as parents or siblings. People who were financially dependent on the deceased, including stepchildren and parents, may also qualify. We'll walk you through who in your family can bring the claim.

faq.q: Is it too soon to call?
faq.a: It's never too soon to have someone protect your family's rights — and it costs nothing. You don't have to decide anything today. But evidence disappears and deadlines run, and we can quietly preserve both while you grieve.

faq.q: The insurance company already reached out to us.
faq.a: Please don't sign anything or give a recorded statement. Let us handle every call from here. Early offers in death cases are made precisely because families are in no state to evaluate them.

faq.q: How long do we have to file?
Will we have to go to court?
faq.a: Most cases settle. But the other side pays more when they know the family's lawyers will try the case — and we do. If we go to trial, we prepare you and stand with you every step.
Nothing up front — ever. We front every cost of building the case and only collect a fee if we recover for your family. No recovery, no fee.
